Subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand the Acme Health use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap of needs:
- Low-latency inference for triage and summarization workflows (target P95 < 350ms for single-request flows)
- Sustained throughput of ~12 QPS peak with occasional spikes to 25 QPS during business hours
- Average request size ~450 tokens in + ~650 tokens generated per request (approx 1,100 tokens total)
- PHI-handling requirement: data cannot leave customer-controlled network for retention/archive; sessions must be auditable

Deployment options we discussed (short form):
1) Hosted API — fastest to production, pay-as-you-go per-token. Easiest operationally but requires sending input to Redwood-hosted endpoints (we discussed options for HIPAA BAA and strict logging).
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools for Acme (single-tenant), predictable throughput and lower effective cost at sustained volume. Redwood manages infra; network can be VPC-peered for transit controls.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — customer-managed control plane or on-prem appliance. Best for strict PHI isolation and compliance; involves license/installation + infra ops on your side.

Immediate ask from my side:
- Confirm the throughput profile above (12 QPS typical, 25 QPS peak) and token averages — I used the numbers above as discussed.
- Confirm whether retention/PHI rule requires never storing logs outside Acme-managed infrastructure (this will determine whether Hosted is a viable path or if Private is required).

Next steps I recommend:
- I’ll pull together a concise cost comparison (hosted per-token estimate vs Dedicated reserved-capacity monthly commitment vs Private license + infra op) and share an Excel with scenario rows.
- Schedule a 1-hr pricing deep-dive next week with Marissa & our finance lead to walk through the numbers and contract constructs (reserved commits, burst options, SLA).

I’ll attach the draft cost sheet to the follow-up once I have confirmation on the usage profile. If any of the above needs correction, please reply inline.

Thanks —

Sarah — thanks for the clarifications; that makes the comparison straightforward. I put together a high-level ballpark to discuss; I’ve attached a short Excel with line items and worked examples ("Acme_Deployment_Comparison.xlsx"). Below are the quick takeaways so you can scan before the call.

Assumptions used across scenarios:
- Pilot volume: 150M tokens/month (input+output combined)
- Peak sustained throughput target covered: 25 QPS
- Target P95 latency: <= 350ms

A) Hosted (per-token)
- List rate example: $0.00080 / token for generation-heavy workloads (note: exact rate depends on model family).
- Pilot cost: 150M * $0.0008 = $120,000 / month.
- Pros: no infra ops, immediate start, flexible scale.
- Cons: per-token spend high at scale; PHI retention constraints unless we enable a private retention contract (adds premium).

B) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — 1-year commit
- Example reserved offer: $50,000 / month for a reserved pool sized to cover sustained 25 QPS of our production profile (this assumes a mix of GPU instances equivalent to 8x A100-class capacity in our performance modeling).
- Effective unit cost (on pilot volumes) estimated ~ $0.00020 - $0.00030 / token depending on instance utilization and batching.
- Burst pricing: additional capacity charged at a blended higher rate for transient peaks (e.g., $60 / hour for extra node-hours).
- Lead time: 1–2 weeks to provision in hosted Dedicated; VPC peering/setup another 1 week for network config + security review.
- Pros: predictable monthly invoice, lower unit economics at sustained volume, managed infra.
- Cons: commit required; spike protection via burst pool with higher incremental cost.

C) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- One-time license + onboarding: $150,000 (covers private control plane + initial 90-day support & runbook).
- First-year infra OPEX (example for on-prem equivalent of the Dedicated capacity above): $45,000 - $70,000 / month depending on hardware choice and support contract.
- Lead time: 6–10 weeks for on-prem install and validation; VPC private deployment in customer cloud can be 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals.
- Pros: maximum control for PHI, meets retention requirements, auditability.
- Cons: higher up-front cost and longer lead time; ops required on customer side for on-prem installs.

Draft SLA / availability notes:
- Hosted API: 99.9% SLA typical for paid tiers
- Dedicated: SLA up to 99.95% with defined failover and capacity guarantees
- Private: SLA construct negotiable (depends on on-prem hardware/support) — Redwood can provide runbook and optional managed-support for HA guarantees.

Attachment: Acme_Deployment_Comparison.xlsx (contains line-by-line cost modeling for the above scenarios with sensitivity rows for token volume and utilization).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync with finance — can we do Wed 2026-04-08 10:00am PT? Marissa & our billing lead will join to walk the sheet.
2) If Dedicated looks promising, we can put a 30-day evaluation commit to lock pricing and start provisioning.

If that timing works I’ll send a calendar invite and the attached workbook.

Thanks —
